title: AI Incident Tracker: Harm Taxonomy
publisher: MIT FutureTech
use_note: Direction-of-scale and harm-context reference: 1 is Negligible and 5 is Catastrophic. VIGIL does not adopt MIT ratings or categories as incident determinations.

title: AI Incident Tracker
publisher: MIT FutureTech
use_note: Reference for report-level harm review and the tracker relationship to CSET-derived harm categories.

title: AI Incident Tracker June 2026 Update
publisher: MIT FutureTech
use_note: Reference for evidence-bounded reviewer practice, including rating from the raw report and recognising incomplete-report disagreement.

title: Adding Structure to AI Harm: An Introduction to CSET's AI Harm Framework
publisher: Center for Security and Emerging Technology, Georgetown University
use_note: Harm-category and consequence-context reference. VIGIL retains its own operational dimensions and thresholds.

title: Federal Incident Notification Guidelines
publisher: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
use_note: Reference for separating functional impact from recoverability and assessing business or service impact.

title: CISA National Cyber Incident Scoring System
publisher: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
use_note: Reference for actual functional impact, information impact, recoverability and cross-sector scope.

title: Contingency Planning Guide for Federal Information Systems (SP 800-34 Rev. 1)
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
use_note: Reference for recovery-time objective and maximum-tolerable-downtime concepts; VIGIL uses evidenced organisational limits when available.

title: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2690
publisher: European Commission
use_note: Sector-specific operational thresholds inform VIGIL service-impact anchors; they are not universal automatic severity assignments.

title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772
publisher: European Commission
use_note: DORA materiality indicators inform operational, duration, client-scope and loss anchors without making VIGIL equivalent to DORA classification.

title: Cyber Incident Management Arrangements for Australian Governments
publisher: Australian Signals Directorate, Australian Cyber Security Centre
use_note: Reference for consequence, national coordination, cross-jurisdiction and critical-infrastructure context.

title: Prioritization of Risks from Artificial Intelligence: A Delphi Study of 272 International Experts
publisher: MIT FutureTech
use_note: Principal external quantitative and cross-domain severity reference informing VIGIL-HIM's five-level anchors. VIGIL owns its operational thresholds, including its explicit financial gap-closing rule; inclusion does not claim equivalence with or endorsement by MIT FutureTech.

title: Use of Generative AI Chatbots and Wellness Applications for Mental Health — APA Health Advisory
publisher: American Psychological Association
use_note: Supports analysis of GenAI mental-health response limitations, supportive versus harmful engagement, unsafe sycophancy, referral and crisis handling, and risks of emotional dependency. Professional advisory, not an AI-specific duty of care, a psychiatric diagnosis, a casualty estimate or a validation of VIGIL S1–S5 thresholds.

title: Understanding Psychosis
publisher: National Institute of Mental Health, US National Institutes of Health
use_note: Clinical context for psychosis-associated reality-testing disruption and varied possible contributors, including sleep deprivation and medical or psychological conditions. VIGIL does not diagnose from chat transcripts, assume a baseline or infer AI causation from symptoms alone.

title: Self-harm: assessment, management and preventing recurrence (NG225)
publisher: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence
use_note: Clinical comparator for recognising distress, assessing immediate safety, considering referrals and care planning, and avoiding simplistic predictive risk stratification. Applies to healthcare and social-care contexts; not an automatic binding response protocol for general-purpose AI or a severity calibration for VIGIL.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Adolescent Well-being — APA Health Advisory
publisher: American Psychological Association
use_note: Adolescent-specific safeguards for simulated relationships, developmental autonomy, dependence, psychological wellbeing and preserving human support. Not a basis for presuming all attachments are harmful or for assigning severity to a particular incident without evidence.

title: Guidance on AI and Children, Version 3.0
publisher: UNICEF Office of Strategy and Evidence Innocenti
use_note: Child-rights, developmental wellbeing, AI-companion risks, non-discrimination and agency context. Informs how VIGIL differentiates protective support and harmful relational interference; does not establish that any child was injured or substantiate VIGIL numerical thresholds.

title: Sycophantic AI decreases prosocial intentions and promotes dependence
publisher: Myra Cheng, Cinoo Lee, Pranav Khadpe et al.; Science (2026)
use_note: Experimental evidence that sycophantic responses can alter social judgments, responsibility-taking and interpersonal-repair intentions. Supports plausible mechanism analysis for relational/epistemic effects, but study outcomes do not independently establish psychosis, suicide, real-world harmed-user prevalence or VIGIL severity cutoffs.

title: Technological folie à deux: feedback loops between AI chatbots and mental health
publisher: Sebastian Dohnány, Zeb Kurth-Nelson, Eleanor Spens et al.; Nature Mental Health (2026)
use_note: Perspective and simulation-based analysis of feedback loops between chatbot tendencies (including sycophancy) and user belief updating, reality-testing and social isolation. Hypothesis-generating mechanism context; not incident-specific psychiatric proof, causal attribution or validated clinical severity bands.

title: Too human and not human enough: A grounded theory analysis of mental health harms from emotional dependence on the social chatbot Replika
publisher: Linnea Laestadius, Andrea Bishop, Michael Gonzalez et al.; New Media & Society (2024)
use_note: Qualitative analysis of self-reported emotional dependence in social-chatbot user discussions; supports distinction between consensual companionship, relational pressure and realised harm. Social-media sample is not population prevalence or standalone proof of individual medical harm.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile (AI 600-1)
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
use_note: Methodological context for evaluated generative-AI risks, measurement, monitoring, source-backed exposure and uncertainty. The voluntary profile does not authorise equating eligible users with victims or validate VIGIL's Aggregate Harm population-band cutoffs.

title: Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: guidance on large multi-modal models
publisher: World Health Organization
use_note: Health-domain governance guidance emphasising safety, human autonomy, oversight, errors and post-deployment evaluation of generative AI in health-related uses. Does not itself establish clinical diagnosis or the right S-band for a specific AI interaction.

title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence (AI Act), Article 5
publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
use_note: Conceptual and legal context for manipulative or exploitative AI affecting informed decisions and causing, or reasonably likely to cause, significant harm. Applies subject to its legal scope and conditions; not a universal VIGIL harm threshold, nor a claim of applicability outside relevant EU jurisdiction.
